## 3. The evidence that moved it




Titles and journals only; no abstracts exist for 2023 here. The strongest item
this month is a refutation and is in section 4(a), where it belongs.

**The neuro-immune interface runs in both directions inside a single month, and
that is the argument for calling it a mechanism rather than a crowded topic.**
[37286594](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37286594/) (*Nature*): activating an
α2-adrenergic receptor triggers immune rejection of tumours — a neurotransmitter
receptor as an antitumour drug target.
[37236193](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37236193/) (*Cell*): the enteric
nervous system is the relay that converts psychological stress into gut
inflammation. Both point neural → immune. Then
[37316669](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37316669/) (*Nature*) points the other
way: dedicated macrophages organize and maintain the enteric nervous system. A
crowded topic produces many papers pushing the same direction, because that is
what a bandwagon is. A single mechanism network produces papers pushing *both*
ways across the same interface, because the interface is real and either side can
be the independent variable. The corpus already read the immune → neural
direction in February ([36640762](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36640762/),
*Cell*, immunity to the microbiota promoting sensory neuron regeneration), so June
is a repetition of that direction rather than a one-off — and this time it is
simultaneous with the opposite direction, in the same journal.
[37289890](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37289890/) (*Science*, flagged by the
journal with [37289885](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37289885/)) closes the
triangle by adding the microbial arm: a microbiota-modulated checkpoint routing
immunosuppressive intestinal T cells into tumours. Neural, microbial and
suppressive-population accounts described as one trafficking mechanism with a
named control point is precisely the claim `neuro-immune-microbiome-axis` makes,
and the +6 this month is not a count of on-topic papers.

**The axis is dosed in patients, twice.**
[36863483](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36863483/) (*Ann Oncol*) gives a
defined microbial consortium alongside checkpoint inhibitors in patients with
advanced solid tumours — the axis tested as a drug.
[36827626](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36827626/) (*JCO*) reads antibiotic
exposure before checkpoint inhibition against overall survival in a
population-based cohort of older adults, which is the microbiome effect measured
at a scale where mouse-model artefact cannot account for it. The standing
objection to this thread has been that dense preclinical publication has no
clinical readout behind it; this month it has two, at opposite ends of the
evidence spectrum.

**Interception gets a randomized readout with ten years behind it.**
[36917758](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36917758/) (*JCO*): low-dose tamoxifen
versus placebo in breast non-invasive neoplasia, holding at ten-year follow-up.
This is drug treatment of a precursor lesion, randomized and placebo-controlled
and followed for a decade — the thread's claim tested the way a therapy is
tested, rather than inferred from a molecular description of a precursor.
[37258665](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37258665/) (*Nature*) supplies the
property the strategy needs to generalize: preneoplasia evolving deterministically
under stringent selection, i.e. a predictable trajectory rather than a stochastic
one, with [37311413](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37311413/) and
[37021392](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37021392/) reading precursor states in
myeloma and pancreas the same month.

**A personalized RNA neoantigen vaccine induces T cell responses in pancreatic
cancer.** [37165196](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37165196/) (*Nature*).
Pancreatic cancer is the hard case for `neoantigen-vaccines`: low mutational
burden, and therefore the tumour where "a large enough and predictable enough
target space" is least likely to hold. A title reporting T cell stimulation is
not a title reporting clinical benefit, and this is an immunogenicity endpoint —
but it is the scale claim tested where it is weakest rather than where it is
easiest.

**One pretrained model transfers to tasks it was not trained on, and two others
predict experiments they never saw.**
[37258680](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37258680/) (*Nature*) states transfer
across network-biology tasks directly rather than assuming it, which is the
`foundation-models` claim in its own words. In the same month,
[37154091](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37154091/) and
[37166159](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37166159/) (*Mol Syst Biol*) predict
cellular responses to unseen perturbations and unseen perturbation combinations.
Three results in four weeks on predict-the-experiment. Read them with 4(a) below,
which is in the same month and does not agree with them.

**What is thin, and what is absent.** `next-gen-checkpoints` takes no card at all
this month. The checkpoint content exists — TIGIT in lymphoma, CD24/Siglec-10,
HVEM/BTLA, CD73 with radiotherapy — but all of it is preclinical or a phase 1 of
a target that predates the quarter, so none of it moves a claim about a *second
generation* arriving. `agentic-ai` takes no card in any of the three months of
this quarter. That is not for want of material about language models: this month
alone carries [37277596](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37277596/) (*Nature*, on
coding with ChatGPT) and [37347992](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37347992/)
(*Science*, on AI distorting human beliefs), and March carried
[36988602](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36988602/) (*NEJM*), already carded
neutral. Across 3,021 titles in this quarter there is commentary about language
models and no paper in which one uses tools, plans, or acts. The thread is a claim
about agents becoming infrastructure, and commentary about a chatbot is not
evidence for or against it. Recorded as an absence, with the caveat that an
absence read from titles alone is weaker than an absence read from abstracts.

**On the meeting in this month.** Section 6 shows 5,757 ASCO 2023 abstracts,
because the meeting ran 2–6 June. The journal papers above are simultaneous with
it, not downstream of it. A journal title carries no submission date and no
presentation history, so it cannot evidence a podium-to-paper interval in either
direction — it cannot show the meeting leading, and it equally cannot show the
meeting trailing. No `clinical-practice` card was written for any month in this
quarter for that reason. A reader looking at a month that contains both a major
meeting and a month of oncology literature will otherwise assume the corpus
measured something here. It did not.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

**TREM2: one target, three directions, one quarter.**
[37001042](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37001042/) (*Blood*) reports that
TREM2 acts as a receptor for IL-34 to **suppress** acute myeloid leukaemia. Eight
weeks earlier, [37081148](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37081148/) (*Nat
Immunol*, May) nominated TREM2 macrophages as the driver of NK cell paucity and
dysfunction in lung cancer — a population to remove. In the same month as the
*Blood* paper, [37601967](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37601967/) (*Cell
Genom*) reports Trem2+ macrophage recruitment predicting failure of cancer
immunotherapy. Three independent groups, three journals, one molecule, and the
therapeutic direction is not the same in any two of them. `suppressive-population-inversion`
claims that depleting a population identified as immunosuppressive improves
outcomes; what this shows is that the *identification* does not transfer across
tumour types, so the depletion logic has no basis for assuming it will. This is
the strongest item in the quarter and it is a refutation, which is the usual shape
of the strongest item on this thread — the supporting side is a genre of target
nominations rather than a set of citable findings, and cannot be carded against it.

[37399355](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37399355/) (*JITC*): an APRIL-based
CAR shows limited efficacy in patients with multiple myeloma, and the title
attributes the failure to the design choice of using a natural ligand as the
binding domain. A negative clinical result that names a generalizable engineering
constraint is worth more to `cell-therapy` than a positive one against a single
antigen, because it bounds a class of designs rather than one product. It sits
against [37188782](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37188782/) in the same month,
which extends the platform to CAR-NKT cells in neuroblastoma; the thread is
+1/−1.

[37248297](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37248297/) (*Nat Med*): translating AI
from development to deployment in healthcare is written up as the hard part, in
the journal that publishes the development papers. `foundation-models` claims
transfer *into clinical use*; this separates benchmark performance from clinical
use rather than treating the two as continuous, and it is the −1 that keeps the
thread splitting despite the month's two supporting cards. Its companion
[37326960](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37326960/) (*Bioinformatics*) asks
whether interpretable deep architectures actually improve drug response
prediction — "myth or reality?" — in the same month as the three
predict-the-experiment results in section 3. Enthusiasm and audit are co-present
here, not sequential.

### (b) Method credibility

[37146621](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37146621/) (*Lancet Oncol*): a review
concluding there is no evidence supporting adjuvant abemaciclib in the indication
it is already used in. This is an audit of registration-grade clinical evidence,
published in the journal that publishes such trials, and it is not alone this
month: [36977286](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36977286/) (*JCO*) re-evaluates
pathologic complete response as a surrogate for event-free and overall survival;
[37172579](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37172579/) (*Cancer Cell*) argues
RECIST v1.1 progression is not the crisp object it is treated as; and
[37338877](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37338877/) (*JAMA*) takes apart the
inference of no-effect from statistically nonsignificant trial results. Four
audits of clinical endpoint machinery in one month. The escalation this thread
tracks — model, pipeline, instrument, assay — reaches the endpoints that decide
what a drug is approved on.

[37198491](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37198491/) (*Nature*): polygenic score
accuracy varies continuously with genetic ancestry. A score reported without the
ancestry of the person it is applied to therefore carries an unstated,
person-specific error — and read with May's
[37388906](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37388906/) on imputation reference
panels, the same structural problem appears twice in six weeks at two different
layers of the same stack.

Two more that did not take cards but belong to the pattern:
[37253541](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37253541/) (*Genome Res*) finds
variants with systematic errors by looking at where genotype discovery approaches
disagree, and [37063090](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37063090/) (*Mol Syst
Biol*) is a multi-site assessment of reproducibility in high-content imaging.
Both are the genre measuring itself, which is the only form of evidence this
thread can accumulate.
